study_sequence.directive: Describe how problems and solutions depend on representing information as data that a computer can process. Summarize the chapter’s points about what representation enables and why it matters for computation.

Explain what “computation” means in this textbook and how computer science frames problems as computable tasks. Include what kinds of problems are in-scope and what it means to solve them with a computer.

Define an algorithm and describe how algorithms relate to solving problems by computation. State the key properties the chapter emphasizes (e.g., step-by-step procedure, inputs/outputs, correctness/termination at an informal level).
Explain the relationship between an algorithm and a program in the chapter’s terms. Describe how a program realizes an algorithm for execution on a computer.

Identify the core components the chapter treats as part of a computing system and how they cooperate to carry out computation. Describe, at a high level, the roles of hardware and software in executing programs.

Summarize the chapter’s view of abstraction layers (e.g., problem → algorithm → program → machine execution) and why abstraction is essential to managing complexity. Provide a short example showing how the same problem can be viewed at different levels.
